'''Geraldine Anne Kenney-Wallace''' (29 March 1943 – 17 October 2023) was a British-Canadian academic.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_JLWAAAAMAAJ&q=%22+Kenney-Wallace,+Geraldine%22+1943 |title = Reports of the President and of the Treasurer|year = 1983}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://umanitoba.ca/admin/governance/senate/hdr/1063.html | title=University of Manitoba - University Governance - Geraldine Anne Kenney-Wallace, D.Sc., May 30, 1990}}</ref> She served as the president and vice-chancellor of [[McMaster University]] from 1990 to 1995. She was educated in England and later earned her Ph.D. from the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.smu.ca/academics/archives/dr-geraldine-kenney-wallace.html |title = Saint Mary's University &#124; Dr. Geraldine Kenney-Wallace}}</ref> Kenney-Wallace was responsible for organizing the first ultrafast laser lab in Canada, in 1974, at the University of Toronto.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.science.ca/scientists/scientistprofile.php?pID=186|title=Geraldine Kenney-Wallace|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=|access-date=September 21, 2016}}</ref> She was a professor of chemistry and physics at the [[University of Toronto]] and had served as Chairman of the Science Council of Canada. She was a recipient of a E.W.R. Steacie Memorial Fellowship (1984), Guggenheim Fellowship (1983), and Killam Senior Research Fellowship (1979). Kenney-Wallace died on 17 October 2023, at the age of 80.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr Geraldine Kenney-Wallace |url=https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/births-marriages-and-deaths-march-11-2024-htbr3spn3 |access-date=11 March 2024 |publisher=[[The Times]] |date=11 March 2024}}</ref>
